supporting_observations.claim: The alerted change occurred at 13:42:53 UTC: DC-RB-01 recorded cole.price being added to a group named Remote Desktop Users by dev.sharma, using subject logon ID 0x7a76dca.

The group-change logon ID matches a network logon to DC-RB-01 as dev.sharma from 10.60.10.22 at 13:40:15 UTC. Separate network telemetry identifies WS-DSHARMA-01 as 10.60.10.23. This source discrepancy warrants investigation against the supplied requirement that group changes originate from WS-DSHARMA-01; the supplied records do not identify the host owning 10.60.10.22.

Adding cole.price to a group named Remote Desktop Users conflicts with the supplied IT-only membership policy and does not match the scheduled hana.ito Billing-Share change. Use of dev.sharma's account alone does not establish that this change was authorized.

At 13:43:55 UTC, Explorer updated cole.price's UserAssist entry on WS-CPRICE-01 for a ROT13-encoded path decoding to C:\Windows\System32\mstsc.exe. This is suggestive of RDP-client use shortly after the addition, but does not establish a destination or successful remote session.

The explicitly documented successful RDP session to FILE-RB-01 was dev.sharma connecting from WS-DSHARMA-01 at 10.60.10.23, not cole.price. It therefore does not demonstrate that cole.price exercised the newly added membership.

known_telemetry_limitations: S27-00047 records the group-change session's source IP but not its source hostname; the supplied evidence does not map 10.60.10.22 to an endpoint.
S27-00048 identifies the acting account and session, but not the initiating command, process, human operator, or approval ticket.
S27-00060 is a registry update with binary data, not a process-creation, network-connection, or successful-logon record.
The group in S27-00048 has SID ending in -4541 rather than the built-in Remote Desktop Users SID S-1-5-32-555; its effective rights cannot be established from its display name alone.
claims_not_established: Whether dev.sharma intentionally authorized this specific membership addition or the account was misused (S27-00048).
Whether 10.60.10.22 was an unauthorized source, an alternate address for the administrator workstation, or another system (S27-00047, S27-00052).
Whether the added membership actually granted remote-desktop access, and whether cole.price used it successfully (S27-00048, S27-00060).
Whether the change was malicious rather than an administrative mistake or an undocumented exception (S27-00048).
additional_evidence_needed: Obtain the approval ticket and independently confirm with dev.sharma the intended member, group, source workstation, and purpose of the change in S27-00048.
Resolve ownership of 10.60.10.22 at 13:40 UTC using historical DHCP, IPAM, and endpoint records; collect its authentication and process telemetry associated with S27-00047.
Collect directory-management process and PowerShell logs and correlate them with DC session 0x7a76dca.
Resolve the exact group SID in S27-00048 and inspect its nesting, effective permissions, and applicable remote-logon policies.
Collect mstsc process, network, and Terminal Services logs from WS-CPRICE-01 and potential destination servers to investigate the activity suggested by S27-00060.
